evidence.title: Vincent Walker
evidence.text: Vincent Francis Walker (born March 2, 1980), better known as Vince Walker, is an American multi-instrumentalist, best known as the lead singer of third-wave ska band Suburban Legends.

evidence.title: Vincent Walker
evidence.text: He was formerly the lead trumpet player, and left sometime after the release of "Rump Shaker", but returned to the band in September 2005 for the band's appearance on the Jerry Lewis MDA Telethon, which happened to be lead singer Tim Maurer's last performance.

evidence.title: Vincent Walker
evidence.text: He replaced Maurer as the singer in an odd switching of roles, and continues with the band as frontman.

evidence.title: Vince Foster
evidence.text: Vincent Walker "Vince" Foster Jr. (January 15, 1945 – July 20, 1993) was a Deputy White House Counsel during the first half-year of President Bill Clinton's administration.

evidence.title: Vince Foster
evidence.text: Prior to that, he was a partner at Rose Law Firm in Little Rock, Arkansas, where he was a colleague and friend of Hillary Rodham Clinton and where, as "The Washington Post" later wrote, he rose to "the pinnacle of the Arkansas legal establishment."

evidence.title: Vince Foster
evidence.text: At the White House he was unhappy with work in politics and spiraled into depression.

evidence.title: Vince Foster
evidence.text: His death by gunshot was attributed by five official or governmental investigations to suicide but several conspiracy theories emerged.

evidence.text: Aaron Bertram, Brian Robertson, Derek Rock, and Vincent Walker appeared on local online radio program "TNN Radio" to announce the album on February 18, 2012.

evidence.text: Charles Vincent Walker FRS (20 March 1812 – 24 December 1882) was an English electrical engineer and publisher, a major influence on the development of railway telecommunications, he was also the first person to send a submarine telegraph signal.

evidence.title: Tim Maurer
evidence.text: Timothy Robert "Tim" Maurer (born October 10, 1980) is an American singer, best known as the former lead singer of third-wave ska band Suburban Legends.

evidence.title: Tim Maurer
evidence.text: He has left the band on two separate occasions.

evidence.title: Tim Maurer
evidence.text: The first was in 2000 after the recording of Origin Edition.

evidence.title: Tim Maurer
evidence.text: He rejoined the band in early 2002 after his replacement singer Chris Batstone left the band.

evidence.title: Tim Maurer
evidence.text: He officially left the band again in September 2005 after the band's third consecutive appearance on the Jerry Lewis MDA Telethon, performing a new song entitled "Moving Closer."

evidence.title: Tim Maurer
evidence.text: The band's former trumpet player, Vincent Walker, rejoined the band for the performance, then took over as lead singer afterward.

evidence.title: Tim Maurer
evidence.text: Maurer returned for a final performance with the band on November 29, 2005 at Huntington Beach High School for a benefit show for the Ryan Dallas Cook Memorial Fund, which was set up following the death of Suburban Legends' trombonist Dallas Cook.
